In just one week, several developments across Europe have raised new questions about the future of the transatlantic alliance. From tensions between political leaders to shifting positions on security and energy, these events may point to deeper structural changes. In this episode, we trace the evolving relationship between the United States and key European countries, examining how domestic politics, energy dependence, and strategic priorities are shaping decisions on both sides. By connecting these developments, we explore whether the West is entering a new phase of realignment — and what that could mean for global stability.
